paper_title: Cryogenic resonant microwave cavity searches for hidden sector photons
notes: Dark photon (hidden sector photon) kinetic-mixing limit from a cryogenic microwave-cavity light-shining-through-a-wall (LSW) experiment. Headline result (abstract, Fig. 5): for m=53 ueV, chi < 1.7e-7. Curve = lower boundary of the black excluded region in Fig. 5 ('parameter space excluded by this experiment is shaded in black'), extracted from the vector fill paths in the arXiv e-print figure chiV2_cropped.pdf (data_source figure_vector). Axis calibration from raster gridlines: x px 263/983/1703 = m 1e-6/1e-5/1e-4 eV; y rows 64/365/666/967/1267 = chi 1e-4/1e-5/1e-6/1e-7/1e-8; cross-checked against the deep resonant spike tip which lands at m~5.3e-5 eV (=53 ueV, detector cavity resonance 12.76 GHz) and chi~1.6e-7, consistent with the quoted 1.7e-7. The steep rise of chi toward low mass follows the (m c^2 / hbar omega)^8 kinematic factor of Eq.1 (single operating frequency 12.76 GHz); a secondary shallower resonance feature appears near m~3.3e-5 eV (chi~2e-6). A small (~20-vertex) disconnected black glyph near m~1e-6, chi~4e-8 was excluded as a stray artifact. Reported chi (not chi^2). This LSW limit is independent of dark-matter density (density-independent), so dm_density_assumed=null. The paper ALSO reports a secondary CDM-halo hidden-photon search (chi < 6.14e-14 homogeneous / 5.32e-15 inhomogeneous at 53 ueV, assuming rho~0.3 GeV/cm^3), but the headline/plotted curve is the LSW result reported here. Confidence level not explicitly stated in the paper; assumed 0.95.
